title: TUI theme
description: The colors and styles a terminal program draws its interface, markdown and code in, keyed by role and tree-sitter capture rather than by any one program's widgets. Every group and key is optional. A missing key falls back along its dots (heading.2 to heading), then to the reader's built-in default, which is written in the terminal's own 16 colors. A reader ignores a group or key it does not know. A change an older reader cannot read gets a new schema URL rather than a version field.

$schema.description: This schema's URL, so an editor validates and completes the file with no setup.

ui.description: The interface's roles: text, selection, borders and the colors that carry a state.

text.description: Ordinary text. An empty style object is the terminal's own foreground.

muted.description: Text that recedes: a hint, a timestamp, a label beside its value.

selection.description: The row or item the cursor is on. Give it a bg, so the whole row reads as selected.

match.description: Text a search or filter matched, usually as a foreground color, so it still reads on the selected row.

border.description: Rules, box edges and the separators between panes.

panel.description: A pane set apart from the main area. Its bg is the pane's background.

warning.description: Something needs attention but has not failed.

markdown.description: Markdown elements, named as Neovim's @markup captures without the prefix (:h treesitter-highlight-groups), so a note reads in a terminal program the way it reads in the editor.

heading.description: Every heading level a heading.N key leaves out.

link.description: A link, where link.label and link.url leave a part out.

raw.block.description: A code block's text where no syntax highlighting applies.

syntax.description: Code, keyed by tree-sitter capture without the @. Any dotted capture may be added, such as keyword.return or function.builtin, and one left out falls back along its dots to the base role.

constant.description: Constants and built-in values such as true and nil.

function.description: Function names, at definition and at a call.

tag.description: Markup tags, such as HTML elements.

color.description: #rrggbb for an exact color, or "0" to "15" for a slot of the terminal's own palette.

style.description: A color and its attributes. A color left out is the terminal's own.

dim.description: Faint text. Its contrast is whatever the terminal makes it.

value.description: A color, which is the text's color alone, or a style object.
